## <b>Agency Information Collection
Activities; Comment Request</b>

<b>AGENCY:</b> Internal Revenue Service (IRS),
Treasury.

<b>ACTION:</b> Notice and request for
comments.

<b>SUMMARY:</b> The Department of the
Treasury, as part of its continuing effort
to reduce paperwork and respondent
burden, invites the general public and
other Federal agencies to take this
opportunity to comment on proposed
and/or continuing information
collections, as required by the
Paperwork Reduction Act of 1995.
Currently, the IRS is soliciting
comments concerning an existing notice
of proposed rulemaking, EE–84–89,
Changes with Respect to Prizes and
Awards and Employee Achievement
Awards. (Regulation section 1.74–1(c)).

<b>DATES:</b> Written comments should be
received on or before April 15, 1996, to
be assured of consideration.

<b>ADDRESSES:</b> Direct all written comments
to Garrick R. Shear, Internal Revenue
Service, room 5571, 1111 Constitution
Avenue NW., Washington, DC 20224.

<b>FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT:</b>
Requests for additional information or
copies of the information collection

should be directed to Carol Savage,
(202) 622–3945, Internal Revenue
Service, Room 5571, 1111 Constitution
Avenue NW., Washington, DC 20224.

## <b>SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION:</b>

<i>Title:</i> Changes with Respect to Prizes
and Awards and Employee
Achievement Awards.

<i>OMB Number:</i> 1545–1100.

<i>Rulemaking Project Number:</i> EE–84–
89 Notice of Proposed Rulemaking.

<i>Abstract:</i> This regulation requires
recipients of prizes and awards to
maintain records to determine whether
a qualifying designation has been made.
The affected public are prize and award
recipients who seek to exclude the cost
of a qualifying prize or award.

<i>Current Actions:</i> There is no change to
this existing notice of proposed
rulemaking.

<i>Type of Review:</i> Extension of OMB
approval.

<i>Affected Public:</i> Individuals or
households.

<i>Estimated Number of Respondents:</i>
5,100.

<i>Estimated Time Per Respondent:</i> 15
minutes.

<i>Estimated Total Annual Burden
Hours:</i> 1,275 hours.

<i>Request for Comments:</i> Comments
submitted in response to this notice will
be summarized and/or included in the
request for OMB approval. All
comments will become a matter of
public record. Written comments should
address the accuracy of the burden
estimates and ways to minimize burden
including the use of automated
collection techniques or the use of other
forms of information technology, as well
as other relevant aspects of the
information collection requests.

Approved: February 9, 1996.
Garrick R. Shear,
<i>IRS Reports Clearance Officer.</i>

## <b>Agency Information Collection
Activities; Comment Request</b>

<b>AGENCY:</b> Internal Revenue Service (IRS),
Treasury.

<b>ACTION:</b> Notice and request for
comments.

<b>SUMMARY:</b> The Department of the
Treasury, as part of its continuing effort
to reduce paperwork and respondent
burden, invites the general public and
other Federal agencies to take this
opportunity to comment on proposed
and/or continuing information
collections, as required by the
Paperwork Reduction Act of 1995.

Currently, the IRS is soliciting
comments concerning an existing final
regulation, LR–218–78, Product
Liability Losses and Accumulations for
Product Liability Losses. (Regulation
section 1.172–13(c)).

<b>DATES:</b> Written comments should be
received on or before April 15, 1996, to
be assured of consideration.

<b>ADDRESSES:</b> Direct all written comments
to Garrick R. Shear, Internal Revenue
Service, room 5571, 1111 Constitution
Avenue NW., Washington, DC 20224.

<b>FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT:</b>
Requests for additional information or
copies of the information collection
should be directed to Carol Savage,
(202) 622–3945, Internal Revenue
Service, room 5571, 1111 Constitution
Avenue NW., Washington, DC 20224.

## <b>SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION:</b>

<i>Title:</i> Product Liability Losses and
Accumulations for Product Liability
Losses.

<i>OMB Number:</i> 1545–0863.

<i>Regulation Project Number:</i> LR–218–
78, Final.

<i>Abstract:</i> Generally, a taxpayer who
sustains a product liability loss must
carry the loss back 10 years. However,
a taxpayer may elect to have such loss
treated as a regular net operating loss
under section 172. The election is made
by attaching a statement to the tax
return. This statement will enable the
IRS to monitor compliance with the
statutory requirements.

<i>Current Actions:</i> There is no change to
this existing regulation.

<i>Type of Review:</i> Extension of OMB
approval.

<i>Affected Public:</i> Businesses or other
for-profit organizations.

<i>Estimated Number of Respondents:</i>
5,000.

<i>Estimated Time Per Respondent:</i> 30
minutes.

<i>Estimated Total Annual Burden
Hours:</i> 2,500 hours.

<i>Request for Comments:</i> Comments
submitted in response to this notice will
be summarized and/or included in the
request for OMB approval. All
comments will become a matter of
public record. Written comments should
address the accuracy of the burden
estimates and ways to minimize burden
including the use of automated
collection techniques or the use of other
forms of information technology, as well
as other relevant aspects of the
information collection request.

Approved: February 9, 1996.
